title: len()
summary: The number of items in a container, in O(1) for every builtin.
description: Calls the object's `__len__`. Builtin containers store their length, so this never walks the collection.

raises.when: The object has no __len__ — a generator, for instance.

examples.title: Generators have no length
examples.output: TypeError: object of type 'generator' has no len()

examples.title: Counting a generator means consuming it

real_world_usage: Validation bounds, progress reporting, and deciding whether to take a fast path.

common_mistakes.fix: `if not items:` is the idiom and does not build an int.

common_mistakes.mistake: len() on a generator or file object
common_mistakes.fix: Neither knows its length. Materialise with list() if you can afford the memory, or count as you go.

common_mistakes.mistake: len() of a Unicode string as a display width
common_mistakes.fix: It counts code points, not glyphs. An emoji or combining accent can be several code points.

performance_notes: O(1) for every builtin container. A custom __len__ can be as slow as its author made it.
security_notes: Check length *before* processing untrusted input, not after.
